alex: quick heads-up — short nsys runs (~1-2s) are biasing kernel selection in our kv-batch path. i saw launch-time variance; sampling misses small kernels.
maria: hmm, which flags were you using?
alex: here's the minimal repro i used:
```
nsys profile --output shortrun.nsys --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=cpu --duration=2s ./run_kv_batch --seq-len 128 --batch 8
```
alex: capture shows big spike from cuLaunchKernel but sample intervals skipped the 3rd kernel entirely — timeline gaps.
sam: can you paste a small timeline excerpt? also try `--sample=none` with longer duration? :thinking: 
alex: attaching excerpt (copied):
```
[0.000s] cuLaunchKernel kernelA 120us
[0.020s] cuLaunchKernel kernelB 80us
[0.040s] cuLaunchKernel kernelC 50us  <-- often missing in samples
```
maria: yeah sampling granularity matters. if kernel < sample-interval it can be invisible. try `--sample-interval=10us` and `--duration=10s`, or bracket the region with NVTX so osrt can trace it deterministically.
toni: another trick: use `--capture-range=nvtx` and put NVTX_PUSH/NVTX_POP around the hot path. osrt adds a tiny overhead but gives exact brackets.
perf-bot: upload complete: https://perf-storage/internal/shortrun.nsys :white_check_mark:
alex: sweet, i'll re-run with `--sample-interval=10us --duration=12s --capture-range=nvtx` and compare kernel counts. will post results.
sam: if small kernels still vanish, run `nsys profile --sample=none --trace=cuda,osrt` for a full event timeline and then slice it — costs more but is ground truth.
maria: note — very high sampling rates + long duration => big file sizes. do this on dev node or smaller batch sizes. also consider `--sample-buffer-size` tuning if you hit dropped samples.
alex: good call, i'll split runs. cc @perf-oncall
